chapter: Minstrel show life and Ida Cox
title: Joining Ida Cox in 1940: St. Louis and Kansas City
summary: With Ida Cox's Dogtown Scandals Review in 1940 he was stranded five months in St. Louis, then worked around Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask about Ida Cox. Did you ever tour with her?
Oh, yes, indeed. I was with Ida Cox in 1940.

That's what I'd heard, yeah. I wanted to hear you tell us about that. We still have time to talk a few minutes about her, if you don't mind. I was with Ida in the 40, and we left away from here. What show was that? Any particular name? Dogtown Scandals Review. Yeah. Where was they located, the winter quarters?
Well, Ida didn't have any special winter quarters then. You know, her home was in Knoxville, Tennessee. Ida Cox.
Well, she didn't have any special place of winter then, I mean because ...
I mean the show, though. Was she just with the show, or did she own the show? It was her show. What was her show?

She had Jack Skank was booking her. Jack Skank was out of New York. He was out of Brooklyn. He and his son was on the show, you know, managing the show. Jew. And I tell you, the show went along pretty good for a while, and we had our bad moments too. Nice, I mean ...

What years, can you figure out about what years? You were with Bessie, that would be in 1937, I guess, when she died. Were you with Ida then, you say, in 1940? 1940. 1940. Did you just start with her then?

Because I was wondering, I first heard Ida Cox in St. Louis, a little theater up in the colored section, in 1938. I happened to be going through, I didn't know she was there. And one night I was walking up the street and saw ... Regal Theater. Yeah, I don't even remember the name, in St. Louis, out there. That's right. Some place I got on Del Mar, out in that section in there somewhere. I don't remember exactly. That's right.
We played the theater again, you see, we stayed there ...
Did you ever go to St. Louis with her? Yeah, we stayed in St. Louis about five months.
Oh really? That's right. In other words, you call me, we were stranded there.
You wouldn't have been there in 1938 then. No, this was in ... I didn't hear you then. That's right, this was in 1940.
Yeah. So we stayed at the Calumet Hotel, on Jefferson. We left St. Louis when we did leave there, we jumped from St. Louis to Kansas City.
Kansas City, Missouri. And we stayed around Kansas City about three weeks, playing in and out of Kansas City.
